target: AG1’s claim that a national Election Day holiday would remove scheduling barriers and enable more people to vote
objection: Even if Election Day is made a federal holiday, many private-sector workers would still have to work because federal holiday rules do not require private employers to close or provide paid time off, so the holiday would not automatically solve their scheduling problem.

target: AG1’s assumption that a federal holiday would help low-income voters in particular
objection: Low-income workers are disproportionately employed in retail and service jobs that are less likely to offer paid time off, so they would still face wage-loss and time-off barriers on a federal Election Day holiday.

target: AG1’s conclusion that Election Day should be a national holiday
objection: A holiday would disadvantage low-income workers relative to higher-income workers because it would help mainly those whose workplaces close or provide paid leave, while many lower-wage workers would still be required to work.

target: AG1’s broader argument that a holiday meaningfully increases turnout
objection: Research indicates that an election holiday by itself is not an effective way to increase voter turnout compared with other voting-access reforms, so the holiday is unlikely on its own to substantially boost participation.

target: AG1’s proposal that a holiday is the right policy response to voting-access problems
objection: Changing state laws to require employer time off for voting and implementing automatic voter registration would be more reliable ways to help people vote than simply declaring Election Day a holiday.

target: AG1’s implication that a federal holiday ensures time off for workers
objection: For many workers, especially in private retail and service jobs, a federal holiday does not automatically create paid time off or workplace closure, so the holiday designation would not reliably change their schedule.

target: AG1’s claim that workers who could vote on a non-holiday day would still be able to vote on a holiday Election Day
objection: When businesses stay open on a holiday, they still need staffing and can deny or limit requests for time off, so some people who could have voted on a normal day by taking limited time off may be unable to do so on a holiday.

target: AG1’s claim that a federal holiday would improve access to voting
objection: If a holiday reduces a person’s ability to take time off to vote, then it reduces voting access for at least some people who otherwise could have voted on a non-holiday day.

target: AG1’s claim that the holiday would reliably remove scheduling barriers for low-income voters
objection: Because federal holiday status does not force private employers to close or give paid leave, a federal Election Day holiday would not reliably eliminate scheduling barriers for low-income people who work in jobs with limited flexibility.
